**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).

Question 8 (a) : les quatre archanges retenus par la tradition islamique sont Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil et Izra'il (ange de la mort) ; le Coran nomme Jibril et Mika'il, tandis qu'Israfil et Izra'il sont connus par la tradition ; le corrigé le précise.
Neutralité : les croyances sont présentées comme celles des musulmans (« Muslims believe », « according to Islamic tradition ») ; aucun numéro de sourate ni de hadith n'est cité.

Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY ». Cette règle (4 questions d'UNE SEULE section) n'est pas exprimable avec `parmi` (un seul groupe) ni `ou` (sous-questions) : `regles_choix` reste vide dans tous les fichiers et la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source ; les références sont limitées à des passages et faits bien établis, les autres points sont formulés prudemment (« according to Islamic tradition », « Muslims believe »). À faire relire par un spécialiste des études religieuses avant mise en avant.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Identify four archangels in Islam. [4 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Islamic tradition, the four archangels are:

1. **Jibril (Gabriel)**, the angel of revelation, who brought the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad and earlier messages to earlier prophets.
2. **Mika'il (Michael)**, who is associated with sustenance and the provision of rain and vegetation.
3. **Israfil**, who will blow the trumpet to announce the Day of Resurrection.
4. **Izra'il (Azra'il)**, the angel of death, who takes the souls of people at death. (In the Qur'an he is called "the angel of death"; the name Izra'il comes from Islamic tradition.)
themes: A Level Religious Studies - angels in islam

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Which archangel is associated with revelation? [1 mark]

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Why do Muslims believe in Archangels? [20 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Belief in angels (mala'ika) is one of the six articles of faith (iman) in Islam, together with belief in God, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and divine decree. Muslims believe that angels are created by God from light, that they do not disobey Him, and that they carry out particular tasks. Archangels, the leading angels, are especially honoured. The reasons for the belief can be set out as follows.

**1. It is commanded by the Qur'an and the Sunnah.** The Qur'an names belief in angels among the marks of a true believer and mentions Jibril and Mika'il by name. The Prophet taught the six articles of faith in the famous account in which Jibril asked him about iman, islam and ihsan. Muslims therefore believe in angels as part of obedience to revelation.

**2. They are the channel of revelation.** Muslims believe that Jibril brought the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad. If revelation is accepted, it is natural to accept the angel who carried it. Jibril is also believed to have brought messages to earlier prophets, and to have accompanied the Prophet in important events, such as the Night Journey (Isra' and Mi'raj).

**3. They show God's power and organisation of creation.** Angels such as Mika'il, who is associated with rain and provision, and Israfil, who will sound the trumpet, show that God manages the universe through the service of His creatures, though He needs no help. Belief in them increases awe of the Creator.

**4. They give meaning to life, death and judgement.** The angel of death takes the soul at the appointed time; Israfil will announce the Day of Resurrection. Belief in them keeps Muslims aware that life is limited and that they are accountable. Muslims also believe in two recording angels who write down a person's deeds, which encourages self-examination and good conduct.

**5. They are models of obedience and worship.** The Qur'an describes angels as constantly glorifying God and doing what they are commanded. Muslims draw encouragement from this example of submission, and they believe angels also pray for believers and support them.

**6. They bring comfort and protection.** According to Islamic tradition, angels accompany and protect people, attend gatherings of remembrance of God and pray for the believers. This belief brings hope and a feeling of being cared for.

**7. Rejecting them would deny the faith.** Because belief in angels is an article of faith, a Muslim who rejects the existence of angels is considered by Islamic scholars to be rejecting part of the revelation. Belief in them is therefore a test of faith in the unseen (al-ghayb), which the Qur'an praises.

**Conclusion.** Muslims believe in archangels because the Qur'an and the Prophet teach it, because they are essential to revelation, creation, death and judgement, and because they offer models of obedience and a sense of divine care. Belief in them forms an integral part of the Islamic faith.
